assembly: Hatch is real wall-mounted geometry, not part of cutout atlas.
Anchor forearm root inside hatch and wrist at fist wrist. Extend wrist joint .06m behind fist to hide seam.
Scale arm along root-to-wrist axis only; keep thickness fixed. Orient cutout plane to camera while its endpoints remain world-registered.
Fist pivots at wrist; scale uniformly. Prefer forearm_a until both camera views validate alternate side. No abrupt view switching.
Drive whole limb in world space from root to wrist; depth-test against real wall/hatch. Forearm should emerge from opening, not lie over wall facade.
On impact lower contact knuckle extent to Y0; derive wrist height from transformed opaque bottom, do not place wrist atY0.
Retreat in world height/depth until opaque fist is above corridor; do not shrink lifted pose to fake clearance.
Keep moving hand visibility independent of permanent opening and use existing event times.
limitations: Two articulated planes cannot reveal a true back surface during arbitrary camera orbit. Scope limited to approved ±18-degree views.
Rendered camera pose, silhouette, wrist seam, contact and clearance must be verified in actual build.

anatomical_alignment.source_axis: Wrist toward palm/knuckles follows increasing atlasY, local sprite -Y
anatomical_alignment.world_target: Project outward root-to-wrist tangent onto camera right/up
anatomical_alignment.pose_consistency: Both poses inherit same axis; no upright reset at switch. Small deliberate wrist flex <=15deg only.
anatomical_alignment.overlap: Transform arm_overlap_px through rolled hand basis, not raw camera basis. Forearm joins proximal wrist along axis.
anatomical_alignment.contact: Recompute lowest rotated opaque silhouette worldY and solve wrist height for contact; old vertical575px formula invalid after roll.
anatomical_alignment.clearance: Use transformed complete silhouette for lift, HUD and wall aperture checks
anatomical_alignment.acceptance: Verify contact and curled poses at both yaw views, plus continuous transition. Previous seam acceptance is not anatomical acceptance.
